symptoms.symptom: Washer Won’t Operate Water Temperature is Incorrect Water Won’t Drain

causes.label: Washer is unplugged
remedies: Make sure cord is plugged securely into a working outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Washer is unplugged"

causes.label: Water supply is turned off
remedies: Turn both hot and cold taps fully on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Water supply is turned off"

causes.label: Controls are not set properly
remedies: Check controls and make sure Cycle knob is pulled out to ON position.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Controls are not set properly"

causes.label: Lid is open
remedies: Close lid and pull Cycle knob out to ON position.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Lid is open"

causes.label: Circuit breaker/fuse is tripped/blown
remedies: Check house circuit breakers/fuses.
Replace fuses or reset breaker.
Washer should have separate outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Circuit breaker/fuse is tripped/blown"

causes.label: Control is not set properly
remedies: Check water temperature control and adjust.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Control is not set properly"

causes.label: Water supply is turned off or improperly connected
remedies: Turn both hot and cold taps fully on and make sure hoses are connected to correct taps.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Water supply is turned off or improperly connected"

causes.label: Water valve screens are stopped up
remedies: Turn off the water source and remove the water connection hoses from the upper back of the washer.
Use a brush or toothpick to clean the screens in the machine.
Reconnect the hoses and turn the water source back on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Water valve screens are stopped up"

causes.label: House water heater is not set properly
remedies: Make sure house water heater is delivering water at 48°C.–65°C.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "House water heater is not set properly"

causes.label: Drain hose is kinked or improperly connected
remedies: Straighten drain hose and make sure washer is not sitting on it.
Top of drain outlet should be less than 1m (3 ft.) above floor.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Drain hose is kinked or improperly connected"

symptoms.symptom: Water Leaks Washer is Noisy Washer Pauses in Cycle Clothes too Wet

causes.label: Fill hoses or drain hose is improperly connected
remedies: Make sure hose connections are tight at taps and make sure end of drain hose is correctly inserted in and secured to drain facility.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Fill hoses or drain hose is improperly connected"

causes.label: Household drain may be clogged
remedies: Check household plumbing.
You may need to call a plumber.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Household drain may be clogged"

causes.label: Constant water pressure to the fill hoses at the water source
remedies: Tighten hoses at the taps and turn the water off after each use.
Check condition of the fill hoses; they may need replacement after 5 years.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Constant water pressure to the fill hoses at the water source"

causes.label: Washer is uneven
remedies: Make sure washer is level and firm to the floor.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Washer is uneven"

causes.label: Washer load is unbalanced
remedies: Push the Cycle knob in to stop the washer, open the lid and redistribute the load evenly.
Close the lid and restart.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Washer load is unbalanced"

causes.label: Shipping rod has not been removed
remedies: Remove the shipping rod on the bottom right side of the washer just before sliding the washer in place.
Do not use the washer with the shipping rod in place.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Shipping rod has not been removed"

causes.label: Water is draining
remedies: There will be a gurgling, “sucking” sound prior to the spin cycle.
This is normal and will stop as soon as the machine goes into the spin cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Water is draining"

causes.label: The washer normally pauses between washing steps
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "The washer normally pauses between washing steps"

symptoms.symptom: Lint or Residue on Clothes Wrinkling

causes.label: Incorrect sorting
remedies: Separate lint producers from lint collectors.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Incorrect sorting"

causes.label: Washing too long
remedies: Wash small loads for a shorter time than larger loads.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Washing too long"

causes.label: Detergent not dissolving
remedies: For best performance always add detergent before adding clothes.
If you use powdered detergent, pre-dissolve detergent in hot water before adding to washer.
Try a liquid detergent.
Use warmer water temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Detergent not dissolving"

causes.label: Overloading
remedies: Make sure load/water level setting matches load size.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Overloading"

causes.label: Too much bleach
remedies: Check bleach package for correct amount.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Too much bleach"

causes.label: Not enough detergent
remedies: Try using more detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Not enough detergent"

causes.label: Incorrect use of fabric softener
remedies: Check fabric softener package for instructions (see Fabric Softener Dispenser section).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Incorrect use of fabric softener"

causes.label: Improper loads
remedies: Avoid mixing heavy items (like work clothes) with light items (like blouses).
Separate permanent press from other laundry.
Try a fabric softener.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Improper loads"

causes.label: Overloading or incorrect water level
remedies: Load your washer so clothes have enough room to move freely.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Overloading or incorrect water level"

causes.label: Incorrect wash and dry cycles
remedies: Match Cycle selection to the type of fabric you are washing (especially for permanent press loads).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Incorrect wash and dry cycles"

causes.label: Repeated washing in water that is too hot
remedies: Wash in warm or cold water with plenty of detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Repeated washing in water that is too hot"

symptoms.symptom: Snags, Holes, Tears, Rips, or Excessive Wear Shrinkage

causes.label: Pins, snaps, hooks, sharp buttons, belt buckles, zippers, and sharp objects left in pockets
remedies: Fasten snaps, hooks, buttons, and zippers.
Remove loose items like pins, objects in pockets and sharp buttons.
Turn knits (which snag easily) inside out.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Pins, snaps, hooks, sharp buttons, belt buckles, zippers, and sharp objects left in pockets"

causes.label: Undiluted chlorine bleach
remedies: Check bleach package instructions for proper amount.
Never add undiluted bleach to wash or allow clothes to come in contact with undiluted bleach.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Undiluted chlorine bleach"

causes.label: Small tears or holes present before wash
remedies: Repair tears and holes before washing.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Small tears or holes present before wash"

causes.label: Chemicals like hair bleach, hair dye, permanent wave solution and toilet bowl cleaners
remedies: Rinse items that may have chemicals on them before washing.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Chemicals like hair bleach, hair dye, permanent wave solution and toilet bowl cleaners"

causes.label: Permanent press items naturally fray (especially collars and cuffs)
remedies: While this is not caused by the washer, you can slow the fraying process by washing small permanent press loads with a higher load/water level setting.
Avoid washing heavy items (like towels) with permanent press items.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Permanent press items naturally fray (especially collars and cuffs)"

causes.label: Some fabrics will naturally shrink in the wash
remedies: Hot water is more likely to cause shrinkage than cold water.
Follow directions on fabric care label.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Some fabrics will naturally shrink in the wash"

causes.label: Not enough detergent (larger loads, heavy soil, and hard water might require more detergent)
remedies: Try using more detergent (especially with larger loads).
If you live in a hard water area try using a water conditioner or install a water softener.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Not enough detergent (larger loads, heavy soil, and hard water might require more detergent)"

causes.label: Water is not hot enough
remedies: Make sure water heater is delivering water at 48°C.–65°C.
Do not use the washer when hot water is used for other needs (dishes, baths, etc.).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Water is not hot enough"

causes.label: Washer is overloaded
remedies: Make sure load/water level setting matches load size.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Washer is overloaded"

causes.label: Soak time is too short
remedies: Soak at least 30 minutes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Soak time is too short"

causes.label: Soaking with too little detergent
remedies: Use more detergent (especially with heavy soil).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Soaking with too little detergent"

causes.label: Detergent is not dissolving
remedies: Add detergent as wash basket fills with water before you load clothes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Detergent is not dissolving"

causes.label: To restore grayed clothes, try one of the following
remedies: Put clothes through a wash cycle using hot water.
(Check the garment’s manufacturing care label to see if hot water can be used.) Add a non-precipitating water softener.
Use 2 1⁄2 times more than is recommended for normal water softening.
Do not use detergent or soap.
Allow clothes to go through a complete cycle.
Repeat if necessary.
Soak your clothes using a water softener instead of a soaking agent.
Allow clothes to soak for about 20 minutes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "To restore grayed clothes, try one of the following"

symptoms.symptom: Yellowed Clothes Blue or Gray Spots Too Many Suds Pilling

causes.label: Not enough detergent on a consistent basis
remedies: Always use the recommended amount of detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Not enough detergent on a consistent basis"

causes.label: Chlorine bleach may yellow some fabrics
remedies: Use non-chlorine bleach.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Chlorine bleach may yellow some fabrics"

causes.label: Iron or manganese in water may cause yellowing or yellow spots
remedies: Use extra detergent plus a non-precipitating water softener dissolved in water and non-chlorine bleach.
Run hot water for 2 minutes to help the pipes clean out iron buildup.
Drain your house water heater occasionally.
To remove spots spread stain area over a pan of boiling water and squeeze lemon juice through the stain.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Iron or manganese in water may cause yellowing or yellow spots"

causes.label: Incorrect use of fabric softener
remedies: Check fabric softener package for instructions (see Fabric Softener Dispenser section).
To remove spots dampen the spots and rub with undiluted liquid detergent.
Rewash, using chlorine bleach if it is safe for the fabric.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Incorrect use of fabric softener"

causes.label: Type of detergent
remedies: Switch to a lower sudsing detergent brand and follow instructions on package.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Type of detergent"

causes.label: Very soft water
remedies: Try less detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Very soft water"

causes.label: Result of normal wear on poly-cotton blends
remedies: While this is not caused by the washer, you can slow the pilling process by washing poly-cotton blends inside out.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Result of normal wear on poly-cotton blends"
